Anna — appreciate the context. I ran a quick availability sweep with the execs and ops team and attached a lightweight availability matrix (demo-availability-matrix-20290610.xlsx). Key thoughts up front:

- True 60–75 min overlap for US(East)/CET/SGT is narrow; windows that touch all three are either very early US or very late APAC.
- Two practical formats we can offer:
  1) One synchronized session that compromises on local convenience (~07:00 PDT / 10:00 EDT / 16:00 CET / 23:00 SGT) — tough for APAC.
  2) Primary joint session for Tom + Priya, plus a 20–30 min separate bridge with Kito (APAC morning his time) — preserves exec time and keeps a full demo for decision makers.

Concretely proposing three DST-aware options (times listed in local attendee zones):
- Option A (single session):
  - US EDT: 07:00 (Jun 12) / CET: 13:00 / SGT: 20:00 — 75 min slot
- Option B (split primary + APAC follow):
  - Primary: US EDT 10:00 / CET 16:00 — 60–75 min (Tom + Priya + Redwood leads)
  - APAC follow-up: SGT 09:30 next morning — 20–30 min (Kito + specialist)
- Option C (UTC-first anchor):
  - UTC 13:00 — we provide converted invites for each attendee; this is the least favorite for internal execs but eases calendar tooling.

I’ve CC’d Lauren (ops) to confirm internal exec availability and to flag any blackout windows (travel / internal all-hands). If any of these look reasonable, we’ll lock invite times and include legal/procurement docs.

Thanks — attaching the matrix.

Best,

Thanks Lauren — small suggestion based on similar tri-zone execs: offer a single "record + live Q&A" option as Plan C. Details:

- Run a pre-recorded 25–30 min walkthrough timed for APAC morning (so Kito can watch live).
- Follow with a 45-min live Q&A anchored for Tom + Priya overlapping Europe and US (tense to mid-morning CET).
- Provide an on-demand short recording for any execs who must miss.

This reduces scheduling friction and preserves the live conversation for decision-makers. Also: beware DST transitions in Oct/Mar (if they ask about recurring cadence), call out in notes that calendar times are anchored to UTC internally to avoid automatic shifts.
